summary: Wall Street erased a violent AI-led plunge (Nasdaq -4.6% at the lows) to close mixed after hot GDP and core PCE kept a December Fed hike ~92% priced; US markets are shut for Thanksgiving today.
events_next_24h: Fri 1:30am USD US Thanksgiving: stocks closed, thin CME futures session
Fri 10:30am JPY Tokyo CPI (Nov) (just after the 24h window)
Forex Factory feed unavailable this run; events from the desk calendar

ES.why: Hot GDP and 3.3% core PCE keep a December Fed hike ~92% priced, and funds sit crowded long (94th pct), but a huge intraday rebound says dip buyers are still active.
ES.risk: A second day of strong dip-buying through thin holiday trade would flip this to neutral.

NQ.why: AI/chip selling (Nvidia -9% intraday) and hike pricing keep the downtrend (-11.6% in 20 days); funds lean long (85th pct), yet the late rebound makes this only a lean.
NQ.risk: Nasdaq reclaiming its pre-selloff level in holiday trade would flip it.

YM.why: The Dow closed +0.3% after erasing a 1,105-point drop; rotation out of tech supports it while Fed hike pricing weighs.
YM.risk: A clean break either way after Thanksgiving would set the lean.

RTY.why: Small caps rose 0.7% on rotation, but a priced December hike is a headwind for rate-sensitive small companies.
RTY.risk: Yields jumping on hike talk would turn it bearish.

NKD.why: The Nikkei is down 8% in 20 days with US tech, but Asia may follow Wall Street's late rebound; funds are neutral (32nd pct).
NKD.risk: Fresh AI/chip selling or a yen spike on intervention would turn it bearish.

6J.why: USD/JPY sits near 159.2 just under the 160 intervention line; Fed hike bets favour the dollar but Tokyo warnings and a BOJ December hike cap it.
6J.risk: Real Japan intervention would send 6J sharply higher.

6E.why: EUR/USD edged up to 1.097 as the dollar index slipped 0.2% after the data, but Fed hike pricing gives the dollar a floor.
6E.risk: A sharp dollar move on post-holiday Fed talk would set direction.

6B.why: GBP/USD was little changed near 1.311 with no UK catalyst overnight.
6B.risk: A broad dollar move would set direction.

6A.why: AUD/USD slipped 0.15% to 0.663, the weakest major, as risk sentiment wobbled, but losses were small.
6A.risk: A renewed stock selloff would turn it bearish.

ZN.why: Hot data argues for higher yields, yet the 10y fell about 3bp to 4.87% as stocks flushed; the two pull opposite ways.
ZN.risk: A deeper equity selloff would lift ZN; hawkish Fed talk would sink it.

GC.why: Gold hit its lowest since Sept 2025 on hike bets then bounced; funds lean short (20th pct), so further downside has less fuel.
GC.risk: A break below this week's low would turn it bearish.

CL.why: WTI rose about 2.5% to ~$84 on reported shipping attacks near Hormuz, and funds are crowded short (10th pct), fuel for a squeeze higher.
CL.risk: Calm in the Gulf and the oversupply story returning would flip it.
